title: Good sheaf dg resolutions and universal tensor acyclicity
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $\mathcal O$ commutative, and use sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and cohomology of cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf of associative unital graded $\mathcal O$-algebras with an $\mathcal O$-linear differential of degree one, $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. A right dg $\mathcal A$-module is a graded sheaf with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^{|m|}m\,d(a)$; left modules have $d(am)=d(a)m+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(m)$. Tensor products mean sheafifications of the balanced graded tensor products, with direct-sum total grading and $d(p\otimes n)=dp\otimes n+(-1)^{|p|}p\otimes dn$. A quasi-isomorphism induces isomorphisms on all underlying cohomology sheaves. Call a right dg module $P$ good if its tensor functor on graded left $\mathcal A$-modules is exact, $P\otimes_{\mathcal A}N$ is acyclic for every acyclic left dg module $N$, and both properties remain true after every base change $(f,f^\sharp):(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)$ of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] and every dg algebra map $f^{-1}\mathcal A\to\mathcal A'$: the pullback is $f^{-1}P\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal A}\mathcal A'$ and the two conditions are over $\mathcal A'$. Every right dg module $M$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $P\to M$ with $P$ good. Good modules are closed under integer shifts and mapping cones of maps between them. If $P$ is good and acyclic, then $P\otimes_{\mathcal A}N$ is acyclic for every left dg module $N$, without a flatness hypothesis on $N$. In the open site of any topological space, the restriction of a good module to any open subspace is good, and restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms and these tensor products. The corresponding assertions hold for left modules with the tensor factors reversed.

source.place: Tags 0FSH (lemma-resolve), 0FSC (lemma-good-admissible-ses), 0FSI (lemma-acyclic-good); definition of good in section-P-resolutions and its base-change condition (3); open localization in section-localization-dg.

proof.text: We first record the closure arguments, not extra assumptions on the site. Call a short exact dg sequence admissible when it splits as graded $\mathcal A$-modules. Tensoring such a sequence with any left module remains degreewise split exact. Thus, if its two outer modules are good, the middle tensor functor is exact: as a graded functor it is their direct sum. For an acyclic left module, the two outer tensor complexes are acyclic, so the middle is acyclic by [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact]. After any base change the graded splitting survives, and the identical argument applies. Hence admissible extensions of good modules are good. Integer shifts are good because they merely reindex the graded tensor functor, and their tensor complexes identify with the corresponding shifts, with signs on homogeneous summands. A cone on $P\to Q$ has the admissible sequence $0\to Q\to C\to P[1]\to0$, so is good when $P,Q$ are good.

source.place: Tag 0FSC (lemma-good-admissible-ses); shift and cone formulas in section-shift-dg and definition-cone

proof.text: Small filtered colimits of good modules are good. Form their colimit degreewise in module sheaves, with the induced action and differential. Tensor commutes with these colimits: balanced bilinear maps out of the colimit are precisely compatible families of balanced bilinear maps, which is the required universal property. The same holds for inverse image, a left adjoint, and scalar extension, by the same balanced-map description. Filtered colimits are exact by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian]. Therefore the colimit graded tensor functor is exact. Applying exact colimits to the sequences defining kernels, images and cokernels gives $H^n(\operatorname{colim}K_i)=\operatorname{colim}H^n(K_i)$; consequently tensoring an acyclic left module still gives zero cohomology. After any base change repeat the argument in module sheaves on the new small ringed site. This proves universal goodness of the colimit, including the sequential colimits below.

For the existence assertion use the free construction [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-free-graded-generators]. Put $\mathcal S_{0,n}=Z^n(M)=\ker(d_M^n)$, regarded as a sheaf of sets in degree $n$, and set $P_0=F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S_0)$. Sending a generator $s$ to the cycle it denotes defines a chain map $u_0:P_0\to M$. The sheafification universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] extends the coefficient-linear formula on the free presheaf. The map $H^n(P_0)\to H^n(M)$ is epi: every cohomology section is locally represented by a cycle, and that cycle has its own closed generator. The cited free-module statement gives goodness of $P_0$.

source.place: Tag 0FSH (lemma-resolve), first proof, construction of P_0

proof.text: Inductively, given $u_i:P_i\to M$, let $\mathcal S_{i+1,n}$ be the sheaf of pairs $(p,m)$ with $p\in Z^{n+1}(P_i)$, $m\in M^n$, and $u_i(p)=d_Mm$. Take $P_{i+1}=P_i\oplus F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S_{i+1})$ as a graded module. For the new degree-$n$ generator $e_{p,m}$ set $d(e_{p,m})=p$ and $u_{i+1}(e_{p,m})=m$, extending by $d(ea)=p a+(-1)^ne\,d(a)$ and $u(ea)=m a$. These formulas commute with restriction and sheafify by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. On $ea$, the two cross terms of $d^2$ have coefficients $(-1)^{n+1}$ and $(-1)^n$, and the remaining terms vanish since $dp=0$ and $d^2a=0$. Also $u(d(ea))=u(p)a+(-1)^nm\,d(a)=d(ma)$. Thus this defines a dg module and chain map extending $u_i$. The quotient is the closed-generator module $F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S_{i+1})$ of [lem-sfb-sheaf-dg-free-graded-generators]; its generators have differential zero modulo $P_i$. The sequence $0\to P_i\to P_{i+1}\to F_{\mathcal A}(\mathcal S_{i+1})\to0$ is graded split, so step 1 and induction prove every $P_i$ good.

Set $P=\operatorname{colim}_{i\geq0}P_i$ and use the induced $u:P\to M$. Step 2 proves goodness. Its cohomology is the filtered colimit of the cohomology sheaves by [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian] and the kernel/image argument in step 2. All $H^n(P_i)\to H^n(M)$ are epi, since they factor the epi from $P_0$. Their kernels are killed by the next transition: a kernel section is locally represented by a cycle $p$ whose image is locally $dm$; the generator $e_{p,m}$ of degree $n-1$ makes $p$ a boundary in $P_{i+1}$. This is a statement about sheaf kernels, so local representatives suffice; no sectionwise exactness or enough-points assumption is used. Exactness of the filtered colimit now gives an isomorphism $H^n(P)\to H^n(M)$ for every $n$. This proves the required quasi-isomorphism, not merely a graded surjection.

The same construction gives left good resolutions. Explicitly, pass to the graded opposite algebra with $a\star b=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$ and the same differential. A left module becomes a right module by $m\cdot a=(-1)^{|m||a|}am$; the Leibniz identities follow by substituting these signs. The reverse conversion uses the same formula. Balanced tensors in the two conventions identify by $m\otimes n\mapsto(-1)^{|m||n|}n\otimes m$; substituting the two differential formulas shows this is a chain isomorphism. These conversions preserve underlying cohomology, graded exactness and commute with inverse image and scalar extension. Apply steps 1--5 to this opposite algebra. Thus the left resolutions needed next are available independently of the tensor-annihilation conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0FSH (lemma-resolve), left-module version via the graded opposite; conventions and signed tensor formula

proof.text: Now let $P$ be good and acyclic, and let $N$ be any left module. By step 6 choose a good left resolution $Q\to N$. Its cone $T$ is acyclic: apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] to $0\to N\to T\to Q[1]\to0$; the connecting map is the cohomology map of $Q\to N$ up to sign, hence an isomorphism. Since $Q$ is left good and $P$ acyclic, $P\otimes_{\mathcal A}Q$ is acyclic. Since $P$ is right good and $T$ acyclic, $P\otimes_{\mathcal A}T$ is acyclic. Tensor the same graded-split cone sequence with $P$; it remains degreewise split exact, with outer terms $P\otimes N$ and $P\otimes Q[1]$. The latter is a signed shift of $P\otimes Q$, hence acyclic. The long exact sequence then forces $P\otimes N$ acyclic. This uses no flatness of $N$.

source.place: Tag 0FSI (lemma-acyclic-good), proof of (1), expressed using the graded-split cone sequence

proof.text: For an open subspace $j:V\hookrightarrow X$, its ringed-topos inverse image is restriction, and extending along the identity algebra map gives $P|_V$ itself by $p\otimes a\mapsto pa$. Thus the universal condition in goodness implies the first two good conditions on $V$; for the universal condition there compose any ringed-topos map into $V$ with $j$, and use associativity $(p\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto p\otimes ab$ of the balanced tensor. Restriction is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-site-restriction-exact], so it commutes with the kernels and images defining cohomology and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Restriction also preserves the stated tensor products: on every open $W\subset V$, the presheaves defining both balanced total tensors are the same; the covers used to sheafify on $W$ are the same on $V$ and on $X$. This identifies differentials and all structure maps. Finally step 6 converts every assertion to left modules with the factors reversed.
